metric_model: CHAOSS AI Alignment - Community Governed Use

scope.note: Scoring confined to the files named on the command line; 'no' means not addressed in those files.

evidence.quote: Contributions must not include content generated by large language models or other probabilistic tools, including but not limited to Copilot or ChatGPT.
This policy covers code, documentation, pull requests, issues, comments, and any other contributions to the Servo project.

Can I submit a PR that includes code generated by AI tools?

No.

Can I use an AI tool to write a new issue description or comment?

No.
you must verify the output of any AI tool before filing issues against the Servo project.

domains.suggested_improvement: no accountability holder named (only enforcement by maintainers)
domains.reasoning: The policy explicitly bans AI-generated code, PR descriptions, issue text and comments, naming code_contributions directly and giving a clear supervision level (banned), with a narrower human_in_the_loop carve-out for verifying AI-assisted bug-finding. However, it never states who is accountable for the output-only that 'maintainers reserve the right to close any pull request' (enforcement, not accountability) and that violating artifacts 'must be rewritten' (an obligation, not a holder). So this is partial rather than fully addressed.

domains.suggested_improvement: no mention of meeting/notetaker bots at all
domains.reasoning: The file contains no reference to recorded meetings, transcription, or notetaker bots of any kind.

domains.scope_or_volume_limits: documentation only named; blogs and design assets not mentioned

evidence.quote: This policy covers code, documentation, pull requests, issues, comments, and any other contributions to the Servo project.

domains.suggested_improvement: no accountability holder named; blogs/design assets unaddressed
domains.reasoning: The blanket ban explicitly names 'documentation' as covered, giving a supervision level (banned) for that sub-area of content, but does not mention blog posts or design assets, and never names who is accountable for content output (only who may enforce/close it).

domains.rationale_only_mention: This is a drain on the (already limited) time and energy of our reviewers.
domains.suggested_improvement: no rule on AI use in moderation actions themselves
domains.reasoning: The 'maintainer burden' rationale describes reviewer time strain caused by low-quality AI contributions, but this is offered as a reason for banning AI-generated contributions, not a rule about whether AI may be used to moderate, triage, or act on reports. No supervision level or accountability holder is stated for moderation actions themselves.

evidence.quote:
Can I use an AI review tool for my pull request?

Yes, but please don't.
The results are unreliable and noisy.

domains.suggested_improvement: no accountability holder named; no disclosure requirement stated
domains.reasoning: The FAQ directly addresses using an AI tool to review a pull request, permitting it while discouraging it, which sets a de facto supervision level of limited/unsupervised use rather than an outright ban or disclosure mandate. It does not state who bears responsibility for a review performed or assisted by AI.

domains.suggested_improvement: no rule on autonomous/agentic action within the repository
domains.reasoning: The page discusses AI tools answering questions or generating content/code, but never addresses an agent acting on the repository on its own (e.g. filing PRs, merging, or commenting without a human initiating each action).

domains.rationale_only_mention: AI tools require an unreasonable amount of energy and water to build and operate, their models are built with heavily exploited workers in unacceptable working conditions
domains.suggested_improvement: no rule specifically governing environmental impact
domains.reasoning: Energy and water use are cited as part of the 'Ethical issues' rationale for banning AI-generated contributions, but this is a justification for the code_contributions ban, not a standalone rule about environmental impact, so no supervision level is set for this domain itself.

domains.suggested_improvement: no mention of server load or hardware/financing strain
domains.reasoning: There is no discussion of server load, hosting cost, or hardware financing anywhere in this file; the closest concerns (maintainer time, energy/water) fall under moderation and environmental respectively, not infrastructure as defined.

domains.rationale_only_mention: Publicly available models are trained on copyrighted content, both accidentally and intentionally, and their output often includes that content verbatim.
domains.suggested_improvement: no statement on Servo's own data being used to train models
domains.reasoning: The 'Copyright issues' rationale concerns models being trained on other people's copyrighted material and reproducing it in output - a provenance concern about code contributions, not a statement about whether Servo's own project content, issues, or discussions may be used to train models.

consent_policy_specificity.overall_posture: The file sets a clear, well-reasoned ban on AI-generated code, PR text, issues and comments (with a narrow verify-before-filing carve-out for bug-hunting and a discouraged-but-permitted allowance for AI-assisted review), naming documentation explicitly within that ban; but it never assigns accountability for AI-assisted output (only enforcement by maintainers), and it is silent on notetaker bots, moderation actions, autonomous/agentic use, infrastructure strain, and the project's own data being used for training - the energy/water and copyright concerns it raises are rationale for the code ban, not rules governing those domains.

awaiting_implementation.specific_tools_in_use: Awaiting implementation: named-product detection beyond known file signatures
awaiting_implementation.ai_tool_owner: Awaiting implementation: ownership and data control
awaiting_implementation.environmental_footprint: Awaiting implementation: model/system card and ESG disclosure
awaiting_implementation.proportionality: Awaiting implementation: resource use relative to contributor count (needs platform usage data)

use_composition_partial.note: Detection only. Absence of signal is not absence of use.

policy_change.blocker: Draft classifier not wired in or validated against hand-graded history. Repo.history() and Repo.commit_patch() supply the diffs.

use_compliance.blocker: Derived metric. Requires disclosed-use data (Use Composition) checked against the specificity grid. Composition is only partially detectable, so the comparison is not yet sound.

misuse.blocker: Not automatable. CHAOSS marks the core signals unknown: text-based AI detectors are unreliable, and license-laundering and wrongful-accusation incidents need maintainer self-report.
